nodes.title: Kernel control calls to the voice runtime with an empty body
nodes.source: main loop (found by the calls and voice builders)
nodes.tried: server/runtime-client.ts control(id, 'end') posted {} to /v1/calls/<id>/end, with the call id only in the path.
nodes.broke: The runtime requires {conversationId, endReason?} in the body. Its HMAC signature covers only the body, so the id in the body is the replay guard. Every kernel-initiated end would have got a 400, and no test covered it: the control plane only ever ran against FakeRuntime, which accepts anything.
nodes.instead: control() always sends conversationId in the body and a caller cannot override it (391f49c). tests/runtime-client.test.ts runs HttpRuntime against a local stand-in of the runtime's HTTP surface, so a seam mismatch fails there and not on a call.

nodes.title: Treating a busy voice runtime as a failed call attempt
nodes.source: main loop (found by the calls builder)
nodes.tried: Campaign dispatch() ran failBeforeRing for every non-accepted start reply, including the runtime's new 503 at_capacity.
nodes.broke: A busy runtime would have marked good numbers failed with provider_error and spent a retry_per_ladder step for each, using up people's retry ladders under load.
nodes.instead: StartReply carries retryable/retryAfterS (391f49c). Dispatch requeues the same attempt after retryAfterS plus jitter, with no failure and no ladder step, and stops claiming for that tick (campaigns, in progress).
